title: Error catalog + runtime hints library for SDKs (retries & streaming ergonomics)
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Create a cross-language "error catalog + runtime hints" library and conventions for Redwood SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go). The goal is to provide a consistent, machine-readable error taxonomy, actionable messages, and explicit retry/backoff hints surfaced in exceptions and error payloads. This will reduce developer confusion, enable automated retry policies, and improve streaming ergonomics (e.g., partial result errors, resumable streams). The deliverable is a small language-neutral specification, reference implementations in each SDK, tests, and a rollout plan that includes a migration compatibility strategy and observability metrics for adoption.
acceptance_criteria: A language-neutral error catalog document (JSON+markdown) listing canonical error codes, human-friendly messages, machine fields (code, category, retry_hint, retryable, stream_flag, docs_url)
Reference implementations in Python, TypeScript, and Go that raise/return mapped exception types or structured error objects matching the catalog
SDKs expose a programmatic RetryHint (enum + suggested_backoff_seconds) and a way to opt into automatic retry middleware that uses the hint
Streaming SDK surface errors that distinguish terminal vs transient stream conditions and include resume token guidance when applicable

End-to-end integration tests that assert consistent error shapes across languages for 10 representative scenarios (rate limit, throttling, transient infra, model OOM, invalid prompt, partial-stream-close)
Telemetry events emitted for each error code with sample rate and dashboards updated to show top error codes by route
Backward-compatible behavior: existing consumers who check only HTTP status or freeform message continue to see reasonable messages; new structured fields are additive
implementation_notes: Define minimal machine schema: {code, category, retryable, retry_hint_seconds, stream_status, docs_url, human_message}
Map existing HTTP statuses + runtime failures to canonical codes; avoid 1:1 with HTTP when richer context exists (e.g., MODEL_BACKPRESSURE vs 503)
Python: implement SDKError base class with attributes .code and .retry_hint_seconds and middleware RetryManager to apply exponential backoff using hint
TypeScript: provide typed Error classes and an ErrorPayload interface; middleware integrates with fetch/streaming client to respect retry_hint
Go: return typed error values implementing interface {Code() string; Retryable() bool; RetryHintSeconds() int} and helper RetryPolicy
Streaming: include 'stream_status' values: partial, resumable, closed_transient, closed_terminal and provide resume_token when resumable
Docs: add migration guide showing how to move from message-parsing to structured code checks and how to opt into automatic retry middleware
Observability: emit metrics 'sdk.error_code' and include 'route' and 'model' tags; ensure logs contain full JSON error for debugging
test_plan: Unit tests per SDK for mapping input failures to canonical codes
Integration tests that inject network failures and assert middleware uses retry_hint_seconds appropriately
Streaming contract tests that simulate mid-stream disconnect and assert resume_token semantics
Cross-language fuzz test: generate errors from runtime and verify each SDK maps to the same canonical code
Add canary tests in CI that run a small app using all three SDKs to validate consistent visible error shapes
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): land spec and Python implementation behind feature flag; run against internal integrations for 2 weeks
Phase 2: add TypeScript + Go implementations; enable automatic retry middleware opt-in for clients willing to test
Phase 3: flip-on opt-out policy (default disabled -> enabled) for non-breaking classes (idempotent calls) and monitor error-code dashboards
Phase 4: publish migration docs, changelog, and deprecation timeline for legacy freeform messages (6 months)
Communication: notify SDK users via changelog, email to active API keys owners, and migration snippet in console
blockers: Agreement on canonical code names and categories from API/product (waiting on product review)
Instrumentation plumbing in backend to attach structured error metadata to responses (infra work item)
Security review for exposing resume tokens in errors for sensitive workloads
